why: AKIEN, 2026-08-19, verbatim: 'logging emissions are supposed to be single json emissions. why are we adding rows to diagnostics.json?' — then, correcting his own framing in the next breath: 'i was expecting to see timestamp.inference.task.json or some such. and i have to be clear, i just created a contradiction. and just noticed it. each call is one task ticket recieving multiple emissions... but for a single inference call.' THE CONTRADICTION HE FLAGGED WAS MEASURED AND DISSOLVES, which is why this ticket is a grain change and not a redesign: across 140 emissions and 68 distinct pointers the gate sequences are only ever miss->hit (66 pointers) or miss->hit->hit->hit (2), and the gaps between two emissions sharing a pointer run min 3.2s, MEDIAN 282s, max 4,348s, with ZERO under one second. Those are separate calls minutes apart asking the same question, not one call emitting repeatedly. One inference call = exactly one emission, always. What made it read as 1:N is that the pointer is the PROMPT rather than the call — it names the question, and a question outlives the calls that ask it — which is the same fact the second half of this ticket fixes. AND HIS OWN STATED WHY IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE CHANGE: the reason he gave for the one logs root on 2026-08-18 was retention, 'easy to delete everything in the logs tree over 30 days old in one go'. A single appended trail CANNOT expire a record — mtime belongs to the file, so the sweep takes a device's whole history or none of it — while a file per emission gives per-record expiry for nothing. breadcrumb_log.py's own 'WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT' paragraph deferred rotation and evaporation on build-minimal grounds, correctly as a policy, and in doing so filed away the fact that the chosen grain could not express that policy when it arrived.
how: ONE writer, ONE reader contract, THREE call sites, and a blast radius counted before the build rather than discovered inside it. WRITER: cairn/tools/base/breadcrumb_log.py — RECORD_NAME and receive_diagnostic's open(..., 'a') become a per-record path; records() sorts the directory instead of splitting lines, and must tolerate BOTH shapes for one retention window because the 1,295 standing records are not migrated (cache-class; they age out where they lie). The stamp in the filename is NOT the record's `ts` verbatim: `ts` is an ISO string carrying an offset and does not sort lexically as time does across offsets, so the name carries a UTC-normalised YYYYMMDD.HHMMSS.uuuuuu — the shape the launcher's boot log already uses, borrowed as a pattern and cited, not grafted. falsifier: FALSIFIER — DONE when all five hold, and each is read off disk rather than off a return value. (1) ONE EMISSION IS ONE FILE: a real inference call (not a fixture) leaves exactly ONE new file under ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/, that file parses whole as a single JSON object, and no diagnostics.jsonl anywhere gains a line in the same window — measured by a before/after directory listing, never by asking the object what it wrote. (2) PER-RECORD EXPIRY IS REAL, which is the property the single trail CANNOT have and therefore the clause that makes this ticket worth its cost: stamp two emission files' mtimes at 31 and 1 days back, run one `find <logs root> -type f -mtime +30 -delete` against the ONE root, and exactly the old one is gone while the young one stands. Under today's shape that same command either deletes a device's entire history or nothing, and the proof must assert BOTH halves so the green is about expiry and not about deletion. (3) THE POINTER IS THIN AND STILL JOINS: inference_domain's emitted pointer falls inside the corpus band measured 2026-08-19 (every other trail's pointer median is 9-70 chars; inference_domain's is 1,171 with a max of 10,078 and accounts for 85% of that trail's 273,421 bytes), AND a record's pointer resolves to its inference_calls row by hashing that row's canonical column — proved against REAL rows already standing in the store, not against rows the proof wrote, because a join proved on self-written rows proves the hash function and not the join. (4) THE READER CONTRACT SURVIVES: BreadcrumbLog.records() returns the same records in the same write-order over the new shape, and cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector/inspector.py reads them with no change to its own logic — the strongest available evidence that the grain moved and the contract did not. (5) THE AGREEMENT TOOTH STILL BITES: the count of gate='miss' emissions equals the count of verdict='miss' rows in inference_calls over the same window, matched by canonical DIGEST rather than canonical text — the substance of the sibling ticket's clause (c), preserved through the vocabulary change rather than quietly dropped by it. WRONG INTENT IF, and both directions are named because the grain can fail either way: reading one device's trail now costs a directory walk measurably slower than the single-file read it replaced at 30 days of records (the measure: time `records()` over a 5,600-file tree against the same records as lines — if the reader got worse, the picture got worse, and that is the parent's own 'logging happened, the picture did not' failure wearing this ticket's face); OR the digest makes a record unjoinable in practice — a pointer nobody can resolve back to its question is worse than a fat one, because a fat pointer is merely expensive and an unresolvable one is a record of truth that has stopped being a record. distinctions_recorded: FOUR, and the first is asked to be ratified rather than merely recorded. (1) A PROVED NODE'S FALSIFIER MAY BE RE-SPELLED BY A LATER NODE WITHOUT BEING RETRACTED, provided the later node's own falsifier carries the earlier substance forward explicitly. an-inference-call-logs-that-it-started proved on 2026-08-18 naming diagnostics.jsonl by name and matching trail-to-meter by canonical TEXT; both spellings change here, its record is not edited (Law 7), and clause (5) of this falsifier is where its substance is carried. Without such a rule the corpus either freezes at its first spelling or a proof quietly stops meaning what it proved. I could not find this written anywhere. (2) BUILD-MINIMAL DEFERS THE POLICY; THE CHECK IT DOES NOT PERFORM IS WHETHER THE SHAPE CAN STILL HOLD THE POLICY LATER. This is the general form of the 'WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT' miss, and it is a real addition to build-minimal rather than a criticism of it: deferring rotation was right, and the grain that made rotation inexpressible was chosen in the same breath with nothing asking the question. (3) FILE-PER-EMISSION IS MORE APPEND-ONLY, NOT LESS. It reads like a conflict with breadcrumb_log.py's 'PURE APPEND, ON PURPOSE, AGAINST BOTH PRECEDENTS' and is the opposite: a written file is never reopened at all, where an appended trail is reopened by every later write. (4) A SHAPE THAT CANNOT EXPRESS EXPIRY IS NOT THE SAME AS A SHAPE THAT HAS NOT CHOSEN AN EXPIRY. Easy to lose, and losing it is how the deferral in (2) became invisible.
